items.title: Boys and Girls Club of Miami-Dade opens Christmas tree lot at ribbon cutting ceremony in SW Miami-Dade
items.text:
SOUTHWEST MIAMI-DADE, FLA. (WSVN) - The Boys and Girls Club of Miami-Dade kicked off the holiday season with a ribbon cutting ceremony at their annual Christmas tree lot in Southwest Miami-Dade.
Shoppers at the store can pick out fresh 14-feet tall Fraser firs and Poinsettia trees.
All proceeds and Sponsor-A-Child donations go toward local youth programs.

items.title: Man arrested in Miami Beach accused of posing as Uber driver, having drugs in vehicle
items.text:
The NBC6 South Florida News streaming channel plays local South Florida news 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
An undercover operation by Miami Beach Police ended with the arrest of a man accused of offering illegal transportation services and having multiple controlled substances inside his vehicle.
The case involves Adrian Manzano, who was taken into custody early Friday morning, Nov. 20, on the 1000 block of Washington Avenue, near the Twist nightclub in South Beach.
According to the police report, officers carried out the operation alongside Miami-Dade’s Passenger Transportation Regulation Division to identify transportation services operating without the required authorizations.
During the investigation, officers spotted a silver Mazda with an Uber sign that authorities say was fake.
An undercover officer accepted Manzano’s offer to take him to the Fontainebleau hotel. They agreed on a $20 payment, and the driver completed the trip. During the ride, Manzano allegedly told the officer he had cocaine, ketamine, marijuana and other drugs.
After dropping the officer off at the hotel, Manzano left the area. Officers later stopped the vehicle in a parking lot on the 4600 block of Collins Avenue.
According to the report, officers initially asked Manzano to step out of the car while they investigated the suspected illegal transportation activity.
However, during that stop they saw two small bags containing a white powder in the driver’s door panel that they suspected was cocaine. That’s when they placed him under arrest.
During the subsequent search, officers reported finding additional bags and containers with substances that could be cocaine, ketamine, methamphetamine, MDMA, heroin and cannabis.
Authorities said the substances were seized and sent to a lab for analysis. For now, the police report identifies them as suspected controlled substances.
Images from the operation also show another person inside the vehicle. In the audio, one of the officers can be heard saying that the person was not the driver’s friend. However, the arrest report does not confirm that person’s identity or relationship to Manzano.
Manzano faces multiple charges related to the alleged possession of controlled substances, as well as accusations of impersonating a ride-hailing company driver and possessing cannabis.
The vehicle was seized and towed by authorities as part of the investigation.
In situations like this, Miami Beach Police remind residents and visitors to use only official apps such as Uber or Lyft and to verify that both the driver and the vehicle match the information on their booking.
This story was translated from Spanish with the help of a generative artificial intelligence tool. An NBC6 digital editor reviewed the translation .

items.title: DeSantis sets special election dates for vacant Senate District 39 seat as GOP primary takes shape
items.text:
Published Nov. 23, 2026, 4:48 p.m. ET | Updated Nov. 23, 2026
TALLAHASSEE, Fla. — Gov. Ron DeSantis has scheduled a special election to fill the vacant Florida Senate District 39 seat, setting up a closely watched Republican primary contest in Miami-Dade County featuring State Rep. Alex Rizo.
Under Executive Order 26-234 , signed Nov. 19, a special primary election will be held on Jan. 26, 2027, followed by a special general election on April 6, 2027, if necessary.
The seat has been vacant since Aug. 25, when former Republican Sen. Bryan Avila resigned after being selected as Republican gubernatorial nominee Byron Donalds’ running mate. Donalds and Avila won the Nov. 3 general election and are scheduled to take office in January 2027.
Candidate qualifying for the District 39 race runs from noon Nov. 30 to noon Dec. 1.
The special election sets the stage for a Republican primary showdown between two Hialeah lawmakers whose House districts overlap with Senate District 39: state Reps. Alex Rizo and David Borrero. Both lawmakers were first elected to the Florida House in 2020 and have already announced bids and opened campaign accounts for the Senate seat.
Rizo, who represents House District 112, enters the primary with major Republican backing, including endorsements from DeSantis, Attorney General James Uthmeier, Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia, incoming Senate President Jim Boyd, U.S. Reps. Mario Diaz-Balart and Carlos Gimenez, and several law enforcement organizations.
District 39 encompasses all or parts of Doral, Hialeah, Hialeah Gardens, Medley, Miami Lakes, Miami Springs, Sweetwater and Virginia Gardens. The district leans heavily Republican, with more than 105,000 registered Republicans compared with nearly 52,000 registered Democrats as of the Nov. 3 2026.

The timing of the April 6 general election means that if no candidate wins outright in the January primary—or if a Democratic or independent candidate qualifies—the district could remain without Senate representation for roughly half of the 2027 regular legislative session, which begins March 2.

items.title: Evermore Bank in Broward to be acquired by expansion-minded Miami-Dade-based credit union
items.text:
Evermore Bank of Fort Lauderdale has been acquired by the decades-old Dade County Credit Union, which intends to expand into Broward and Palm Beach counties.

Evermore Bank of Fort Lauderdale, one of the area’s youngest commercial banks, will soon be taken over by the Dade County Federal Credit Union, a deal that will give the latter institution new physical locations in Broward and Palm Beach counties.
Evermore opened its doors in December 2022, and maintains branches at 3696 N. Federal Highway in Fort Lauderdale, and at 11940 Federal Highway in Palm Beach Gardens. Its dissolution would lessen an already thin population of community banks in Broward County.
The two sides did not disclose the purchase price. But they said their boards of directors unanimously approved the takeover agreement, which still requires shareholder and regulatory approvals.
Once the deal is closed next year, Evermore would disappear and its remaining assets would be distributed to shareholders, according to the announcement.
“This agreement represents an exciting new chapter for Dade County Federal Credit Union and the communities we serve,” said George Joseph, the credit union’s president and CEO.
Federica Chalumeau, chief experience officer for the credit union, told the South Florida Sun Sentinel on Monday that the customer transition from Evermore to the credit union would be automatic, with the Evermore customers becoming credit union members.
“In June 2027 we are hiring a firm that is going to help us with the conversion,” she said. “There is nothing for Evermore customers to do. We are all about taking our time with this merger, doing it right instead of doing it fast.”
Steven Sanzone, the CEO of Evermore, said in the announcement that his bank’s customers would gain access to additional products, services and resources as a result of the deal. He was unavailable for comment on Monday.
Chalumeau said the credit union offers a wide array of loans, helping members finance autos, boats and homes, among other purchases. It also offers home equity lines of credit, personal loans and consumer credit cards. It also operates a concierge vehicle search service for members seeking to buy cars.
“You tell us the make, model and color — new or used — and we shop the market for you,” she said.
Founded on May 1, 1939, Dade County Federal Credit Union opened to provide financial services to county employees.
Two years ago, the credit union obtained permission from the National Credit Union Administration to seek members from outside Miami-Dade, an initiative that took hold in Broward in 2024; at the end of last year the credit union received approval for Palm Beach and Monroe counties.
“We already have a location in Pembroke Pines,” Chalumeau said. “We will be opening in Palm Beach [County] in July.”
The latter location is at 374 Northlake Blvd. in North Palm Beach, just 3.1 miles away from the branch currently operated by Evermore.

items.title: 1836: Dade County is created
items.desc: Dade County was created on February 4, 1836, named after Major Francis L. Dade and the Miami River. That same year, Fort Dallas was built and served as a military base during the Second Seminole War.
